author: Bay State News
title: UMass baseball loses to Harvard 17-12 in Beanpot consolation game
text:
The University of Massachusetts baseball team lost to Harvard, 17-12, in the Beanpot Consolation at Harrington Athletics Village on Tuesday afternoon, April 14.
The result moves UMass to a season record of 9-19 while Harvard improves to 7-19. The game saw high offensive output from both teams and multiple lead changes.
Anthony Tirado, Ty Fox, and Vance Bonior each collected three hits for UMass. Gavin O’Brien and Sam Hill added two hits apiece. Tirado and Hill each scored three runs; Bonior scored twice. Fox and Hill drove in three runs each, with O’Brien and Braden Sullivan adding two runs batted in apiece.
Harvard took an early lead by scoring four runs in the first inning and three more in the second for a quick 7-0 advantage. UMass responded with two runs in the third inning after Ty Fox singled home Sam Hill and Anthony Tirado. In the fourth inning, Massachusetts tied the game at seven with five runs fueled by contributions from several players including Sullivan’s two-run single.
Harvard regained control by scoring four times in the fifth inning—highlighted by a three-run home run—and added another run in the seventh to go up 12-7. Both teams put up five runs each during an eighth-inning rally that left Harvard ahead, 17-12.
Lorcan Lee (0-3) took the loss for UMass after allowing five runs over 3.2 innings pitched while Daniel Sams (1-1) earned the win for Harvard with a scoreless relief appearance over nearly three innings.
UMass will return to conference play hosting Bowling Green for a three-game series starting Friday, April 17 through Sunday, April 19. All games are scheduled to be streamed on ESPN+.
